quotes.text: 2. This was the first building and second property acquired by the National Trust. It has a stone tablet on it recording that "The old Vicarage of Alfriston, which had fallen into decay, was bought and repaired by the National Trust, 1898". C14 timber-framed and close-studded building of wealden type with plaster infilling. Each end projects, the first floor of the east projection oversailing on brackets. Curved braces and brackets to eaves of recessed centre. Ripped thatched roof. Casement windows with diamond-shaped panes, one being an oriel. Brick chimney breast on west wall. The interior retains its open hall with crown-post exposed.

note: Tranche 3, English medieval fabric and the Tudor house, 5 Sep 2026. THE ENTRY STATES NO NUMBER AT ALL AND THIS RECORD THEREFORE CARRIES NO MEASUREMENTS -- the dominant outcome of a European list entry for a small house, recorded rather than filled. 'Ripped thatched roof' is printed exactly so in the legacy text and is almost certainly a transcription of 'Hipped'; it is kept verbatim and read nowhere. The entry independently confirms the two things the node's own prose leans on -- the Wealden type and the open hall with its crown post.
